title: Slash Commands & Skills
description: Built-in commands, your own reusable commands, and skills Claude loads on demand.

theory.title: The built-in toolbox
theory.body:
Type `/` in a session to open the command menu. A few Kip uses daily:

`/clear` starts a fresh conversation, `/compact` summarizes it to free context, `/init` creates a `CLAUDE.md`, `/model` switches models, `/rewind` rolls back to an earlier point, `/usage` (alias `/cost`) shows usage, and `/help` lists everything.

theory.title: Write your own
theory.body:
A custom command is just a Markdown file. Put `fix-issue.md` in `.claude/commands/` (project, shared) or `~/.claude/commands/` (personal) and you get `/fix-issue`.

`$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with whatever you type after the command. Optional frontmatter adds `description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools` and `model`.

Commands have been merged into **skills**, but `.claude/commands/` files keep working.
theory.code:
---
description: Fix a GitHub issue by number
argument-hint: [issue-number]
---
Fix issue #$ARGUMENTS. Read the issue, find the root cause,
write a failing test, then fix it.

exercises.prompt: Match each built-in command to what it does.

pairs.right: Roll back to an earlier point

exercises.explanation: Built-in commands control the session itself rather than asking Claude to do work.

exercises.prompt: Your context is filling up but you want to keep the same conversation going. Free up space.
exercises.explanation: `/compact` summarizes the conversation so far, while `/clear` would start over.

exercises.prompt: Generate a CLAUDE.md guide for this project.
exercises.explanation: `/init` initializes the project with a CLAUDE.md file.

exercises.prompt: You create `.claude/commands/fix-issue.md`. How do you run it?
exercises.explanation: The file name without `.md` becomes the command name.

exercises.prompt: Complete this command file so it shows a description and passes the file path through.
exercises.code:
---
___: Write unit tests for a file
argument-hint: [file-path]
---
Write thorough unit tests for $___.
Cover edge cases and run the test suite afterwards.
exercises.explanation: `description` labels the command and `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with what you type after it.

exercises.prompt: Your project has a /fix-issue command. Run it for issue 482.
exercises.hint: Type the command, then the argument.
exercises.explanation: Everything after the command name becomes `$ARGUMENTS`.

exercises.prompt: Where do you put a command you want available in ALL your projects?
exercises.explanation: The `~/.claude/` folder holds personal configuration that follows you across projects.

exercises.prompt: Which body makes a better /review-diff command?
options: Review the staged diff for bugs, missing tests and security issues. Focus on $ARGUMENTS if provided. List findings by severity with file:line references.
exercises.explanation: A reusable command should spell out scope, criteria and output format once, so every run is consistent.

steps: Add changelog.md with a description in frontmatter
Write the instructions, using $ARGUMENTS for the version
Commit the file so teammates get it too
exercises.explanation: A command is just a committed Markdown file, so sharing it is a normal git commit.

theory.title: What is a skill?
theory.body:
A **skill** is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file: YAML frontmatter plus Markdown instructions. Put it in `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project) or `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (personal).

Claude reads each skill's `description` and **loads the skill automatically when it is relevant**. You can also invoke it yourself with `/skill-name`. Because it is a folder, a skill can bundle extra files like scripts and templates.
theory.code:
---
name: release-notes
description: Drafts release notes from merged PRs. Use when the
  user asks for a changelog or release notes.
---
1. List PRs merged since the last tag.
2. Group them into Features, Fixes and Chores.

theory.title: Who gets to trigger it
theory.body:
`disable-model-invocation: true` means only **you** can invoke the skill (great for `/deploy`). `user-invocable: false` means only **Claude** can.

`/skills` lists the skills available in this session. A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy`; skills are recommended for new work because they support extra files.

exercises.prompt: Where does a project skill named `pdf-forms` live?
exercises.explanation: Each skill is a folder named after it, containing SKILL.md.

exercises.prompt: What does Claude use to decide whether to load a skill automatically?
exercises.explanation: The description tells Claude what the skill does and when to use it.

exercises.prompt: Finish this SKILL.md so Claude knows when to use it, but only you can trigger it.
exercises.code:
---
name: deploy
___: Deploys the app to staging. Use when the user asks to deploy.
disable-model-invocation: ___
---
Run the deploy script and report the URL.
exercises.explanation: `description` explains the skill and `disable-model-invocation: true` stops Claude from invoking it on its own.

exercises.prompt: Match each skill piece to its role.

pairs.right: Tells Claude when to use it

exercises.explanation: Frontmatter fields control discovery and who can trigger a skill.

exercises.prompt: List the skills available in this session.
exercises.hint: Plural of what you are listing.
exercises.explanation: `/skills` lists available skills and lets you filter them.

exercises.prompt: Which skill description will help Claude load it at the right moment?
options: description: Generates Prisma migration files. Use when the user asks to change the database schema or add a table.
exercises.explanation: Claude matches tasks against the description, so say what it does and when to use it.

exercises.prompt: Build a project skill for writing API docs.
steps: Write SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter
Add instructions, plus any helper script in the folder
Ask for API docs, or type /api-docs
Check that Claude followed the skill's steps
exercises.explanation: A skill is a folder with SKILL.md, triggered by a matching task or by name.

exercises.prompt: What can a skill do that a single command file cannot?
options: Bundle supporting files like scripts and templates in its folder
exercises.explanation: A skill is a directory, so it can carry extra resources alongside SKILL.md.

exercises.scenario: Ask Claude to create a project skill that writes commit messages following your team's Conventional Commits rules.
exercises.sample: Create a project skill at .claude/skills/commit-message/SKILL.md. Base the rules on the commit section of @CONTRIBUTING.md (Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary, max 72 chars, body explains why). Give it a description that says to use it whenever I ask for a commit message, and include two good examples.
exercises.explanation: A good skill request names the location, the source of the rules, and a description that triggers at the right time.

mission.title: Command Crafter
mission.intro: Kip keeps a toolbelt of tricks. Build your first custom command and skill in a real repo.
checklist: Type `/` in a session and browse the built-in command menu
Create `.claude/commands/standup.md` that summarizes recent git commits, using `$ARGUMENTS` for the time range
Run `/standup yesterday` and tweak the file until the output is useful
Create `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a clear description, then ask a task that matches it
Run `/skills` to confirm your skill is listed
mission.explanation: Reusable commands and skills turn your best prompts into one-keystroke tools.

cheatsheet.description: Open the command menu; type letters to filter.
Start a new conversation with empty context.
Summarize the conversation to free up context.
Create a CLAUDE.md guide for the project.
Roll conversation and/or code back to an earlier point.
Replaced with everything typed after the command name.
Project skill: frontmatter plus instructions, loaded when relevant.
List skills available in this session.
Set true so only you can invoke the skill.
Autocomplete hint showing the expected arguments.
